correctness.rationale: Signed coordinate permutations reduce Nλ²/E² to Qλ(t)=[λ+(1+t)²]/(1+t²), 0≤t≤1. Its derivative 2(1−λt−t²)/(1+t²)² has one interior maximum at tλ=(sqrt(λ²+4)−λ)/2; minima are endpoint axes for λ≤2 and diagonals for λ≥2, yielding Mλ and mλ. Any Euclidean pullback quadratic comparison can be averaged over the norm’s eight true isometries, preserving bounds and producing a scalar Euclidean form, so the coordinate Euclidean comparator is globally Banach–Mazur optimal. Euclidean Ptolemy supplies upper C_Pt≤M/m, and two explicit x,y,z triples attain it in the respective λ regimes. Independent direct norm evaluation at λ=0.1,1,2,2.5,5,50 reproduced exact M/m to <5e−16. This covers λ=2 and all λ>0 analytically; no interior-exponent theorem is asserted.

originality.rationale: Yang’s fully inspected Theorem 2.2 gives the SAME two-branch value for Jordan–von Neumann constant, so C_NJ itself is not new. Zuo 2012 supplies comparison methods and Zuo 2018 treats other comparable/midpoint-exponent cases and expressly identifies mixed cross-exponent exact Ptolemy constants as unresolved. Their general theorems require one-sided and/or midpoint behavior that fails for the present sharp off-midpoint ratio; even λ≤2, the theorem-8 fψ range condition is not satisfied at the required value. The accepted added mathematical facts are the exact sharp Ptolemy witness and optimal Banach–Mazur equality for all λ, not the known numerical expression alone. No inspected source implies those assertions, but later unindexed overlap remains possible.
residual_risks: Exact Jordan–von Neumann formula is known from Yang (2015) and is not new.
An unindexed later mixed-plane Ptolemy computation may already treat the λ endpoint; priority is best of knowledge.
No claim beyond real dimension two and cross-exponent endpoint p=1,q=∞.
